claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a single-phase, homogeneous simple solid solution after homogenization annealing.
The simple solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi structure has low lattice distortion.
The homogeneous, low-lattice-distortion structure provides few barriers to dislocation motion.
Dislocations glide easily in the as-annealed simple solid-solution alloy under load.
Dynamic recovery activates early during deformation of the alloy.
Easy dislocation glide and early dynamic recovery cause low work hardening.
Low work hardening and weak impediment of dislocation motion account for the alloy's relatively low hardness and strength.
Uniformly distributed solute atoms do not generate strong local lattice strains in this alloy.
The absence of secondary phases removes precipitate-based barriers to dislocation motion.
Dislocations undergo recovery or recombination with little net accumulation during deformation.
Easy dislocation motion permits the alloy to retain favorable plasticity and machinability despite its low hardness and moderate strength.
Pre-deformation increases the dislocation density and introduces additional obstacles to subsequent dislocation motion.
Controlled aging can promote precipitate formation and thereby introduce dislocation obstacles.
The as-annealed alloy will have lower yield strength than a cold-worked or aged state containing enhanced dislocation obstacles.
The as-annealed alloy will have lower hardness than a cold-worked or aged state containing enhanced dislocation obstacles.
In-situ TEM deformation of the as-annealed state will show easy dislocation motion with little pile-up or strong pinning.
The proposed behavior is expected under room-temperature, quasi-static loading at a moderate strain rate.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at high strain rates, extreme temperatures, or after processing that creates secondary phases.
Significant pile-up or strong solute- or precipitate-based pinning in the as-annealed state would falsify the proposed easy-glide mechanism.
Failure of pre-deformation to produce any measurable increase in strength or hardness would be treated as falsifying the proposed mechanism.
